concepts.name: Preterite vs imperfect
concepts.verify_guidance: A preterite for a background state, a reason (porque tuve miedo), age, clock or scheduled time, a description or an identity (la pistola fue un juguete; descubrieron que ella fue la princesa) is a clear error unless the text itself marks a bounded episode (an explicit end or closed duration, de repente, a change of state). A preterite inside an explicit habitual frame (siempre, cada, todos los días, cuando éramos niños, a run of parallel imperfects) is a clear error. An imperfect for a single foregrounded event in a one-off story (cuando llegaba a casa for one arrival; empezábamos for the first event) is a clear error. Preterite saber, conocer, querer, poder change meaning (supe = found out, quise = tried or decided); where the context means the state, the preterite is a clear error.

concepts.name: Por vs para
concepts.verify_guidance: Do not construct a cause or motive reading of por when the obvious meaning is a purpose, goal, recipient or deadline (no estudio por las clases, hacer un pastel por su madre, delgada por el verano: all need para). Para with a person who is the intended recipient or for whom something is suitable is acceptable; por for a person is acceptable when the meaning is for their sake, in support of, or in their place.
